memories.text: User always wants spoken answers to be short
The ROV control board is an Arduino Nano and a second Nano reads the sensors
The ROV tether uses RS485 between the surface box and the vehicle
Propulsion on the ROV is four Blue Robotics T200 thrusters
PHYSIX is a browser-based physics simulator and the flagship of SimVerse Lab
SimVerse Lab is hosted on Strato and the domain is simverselab.com
HexVault is a 3D printing product line sold on Etsy
The Ender 3 printer needs a 60 degree bed for PETG and 80 degrees for ABS
The home lab is a 15 square metre room that doubles as a workshop
Heat exchanger assignment 6BPR02 cools ethanol with river water in a shell and tube design
The Nanomaterials exam 6E12X0 covers nanoparticle synthesis and characterization
The user's favourite programming language is Python
Daily summary 2026-11-10: decided on RS485 for the ROV tether and ordered the T200 thrusters
The ROV depth sensor wiring is in progress on the bench

files.rov/README.md:
# ROV

Underwater vehicle with two Arduino Nano boards.

## Wiring

The depth sensor (MS5837) connects to the sensor Nano on pins A4 and A5 over I2C. Power it from 3.3V.
api_key = SHOULD_NOT_BE_INDEXED

## Tether

RS485 over Cat6 cable with a 120 ohm termination resistor at both ends.
files.notes/printing.md:
# Printing notes

## PETG

Bed 60C, nozzle 235C, part fan 40 percent. Dry the filament first.

## ABS

Bed 80C, nozzle 250C, no fan, use an enclosure.
